label: prp-curve
title: Proposition
body_md:
\protect\hypertarget{prp-curve}{}\label{prp-curve}

Suppose \(F\) is continuously differentiable and \(J(s)\) is nonsingular
on an interval \(\mathcal S\) containing the truth. Then there is a
continuously differentiable curve
\(s\mapsto\theta(s)=\{\beta(s),\gamma_0(s),\gamma_X(s),s\}\),
\(s\in\mathcal S\), unique in a neighborhood of the truth, along which
all moments of (\ref{eq-moments}) except the \(Z\)-coordinate vanish
identically.
head: environment
name: The identified curve

title: Proof
body_md:
\(F\) vanishes at the truth by construction. The implicit function
theorem applied at that point gives a unique continuously differentiable
solution \((\beta,\gamma_0,\gamma_X)(s)\) locally, with derivative
\(-J(s)^{-1}\partial F/\partial s\); nonsingularity of \(J\) throughout
\(\mathcal S\) extends the solution along \(\mathcal S\) by
continuation---the set of \(s\) reached is open by the same theorem and
closed because \(J\) is nonsingular at its boundary points, hence all of
the interval \(\mathcal S\)---on which the moments remain finite by
Condition \ref{def-mgf}.
head: environment

label: lem-signal
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: The identifying signal factorizes through the relevance

title: Proof
body_md:
\(g_Z=(R/\pi_\gamma-1)Z\) and \(E\{(R/\pi_\gamma-1)\nu\}=0\) because
\(\nu\) is independent of \((X,Y,R)\) with mean zero; the remaining term
is \(\rho E\{(R/\pi_\gamma-1)S\}\), which does not involve \(\rho\). Two
things are needed for that last clause: the joint law of \((X,Y,R,S)\)
is free of \(\rho\), since (\ref{eq-relevance}) fixes only the
conditional law of \(Z\); and so is the curve, since the moments that
determine it do not involve \(Z\).
head: environment

label: def-overlap
title: Condition
head: environment
name: Overlap

label: def-mgf
title: Condition
head: environment
name: Moments

label: lem-intercept
title: Lemma
body_md:
\protect\hypertarget{lem-intercept}{}\label{lem-intercept}

Under Conditions \ref{def-overlap} and \ref{def-mgf},
\(E(\pi_0/\pi_\gamma)=1\) if and only if
\(\gamma_0=\log E(\pi_0e^{-w})-\log\{\operatorname{pr}(R=0)\}\).
head: environment
name: Closed form for the intercept

title: Proof
body_md:
\(\pi_0/\pi_\gamma=\pi_0+e^{-\gamma_0}\pi_0e^{-w}\); take expectations
and use \(E(\pi_0)=\operatorname{pr}(R=1)\), so that
\(e^{-\gamma_0}E(\pi_0e^{-w})=\operatorname{pr}(R=0)\), and solve for
\(\gamma_0\). Both sides are strictly positive by Condition
\ref{def-overlap}, which gives \(E(\pi_0e^{-w})>0\) from \(\pi_0>0\) and
\(\operatorname{pr}(R=0)>0\) from \(\pi_0<1\), so the logarithm is
available; \(e^{-\gamma_0}\) is strictly monotone, so the solution is
unique.
head: environment

label: thm-decomposition
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Exact decomposition of the inverse-weight second moment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since \(\pi_\gamma\) is a function of \((Y,X)\), conditioning gives
\(E(R/\pi_\gamma^{2})=E(\pi_0/\pi_\gamma^{2})\). Expand
\(E\{\pi_0(1+e^{-(\gamma_0+w)})^2\}\) and substitute
Lemma~\ref{lem-intercept}; the third term is finite by Condition
\ref{def-mgf}.
head: environment

label: cor-ess
title: Corollary
head: environment
name: Effective sample size

title: Proof
body_md:
\(n^{-1}\sum_i\omega_i\to_pE(R/\pi_\gamma)=1\) by
Lemma~\ref{lem-intercept} and
\(n^{-1}\sum_i\omega_i^{2}\to_pE(R/\pi_\gamma^{2})\); apply the
continuous mapping theorem and substitute (\ref{eq-decomposition}).
head: environment

label: cor-ess-bound
title: Corollary
head: environment
name: The effective sample size never exceeds the respondents

title: Proof
body_md:
By (\ref{eq-chisq}) the smallest possible value of \(\Lambda\) is
\(1/p\) with \(p=\operatorname{pr}(R=1)\), attained when \(w\) is
degenerate. Substituting into (\ref{eq-ess}) and writing \(q=1-p\), the
denominator becomes \(p+2q+q^{2}/p=(p+q)^{2}/p=1/p\), so
\(\mathrm{ESS}\le np\). Any departure of \(w\) from degeneracy increases
\(\Lambda\) and so decreases the effective sample size.
head: environment

label: thm-integral
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Integral representation

title: Proof
body_md:
Put \(f(T)=K(2T)-2K(T)=\log\Lambda(T)\). Then \(f(0)=f'(0)=0\) and
\(f''(T)=4K''(2T)-2K''(T)\); apply Taylor's theorem with integral
remainder.
head: environment

label: cor-gaussian
title: Corollary
body_md:
\protect\hypertarget{cor-gaussian}{}\label{cor-gaussian}

If \(W\) is Gaussian with variance \(v\), then
\(\operatorname{var}_s(W)=v\) for all \(s\) and
\(\log\Lambda(T)=vT^{2}\) exactly.
head: environment
name: Gaussian case

label: cor-sandwich
title: Corollary
head: environment
name: Sandwich

title: Proof
body_md:
Both follow from (\ref{eq-integral}) by bounding its integrand. A
Gaussian law tilted by \(e^{sW}\) is Gaussian with the same variance, so
\(\operatorname{var}_s(W)\equiv v\), the integrand is \(4v-2v=2v\), and
\(\int_0^T(T-s)2v\,ds=vT^{2}\). Under the sandwich the integrand lies
between \(4v_--2v_+\) and \(4v_+-2v_-\), and
\(\int_0^T(T-s)\,ds=T^{2}/2\) gives the two bounds.
head: environment

label: cor-atom
title: Corollary
body_md:
\protect\hypertarget{cor-atom}{}\label{cor-atom}

Let \(W\) have essential supremum \(M_W<\infty\) and suppose it carries
an atom there, \(\operatorname{pr}(W=M_W)>0\). Then
\(\log\Lambda(T)\to-\log\operatorname{pr}(W=M_W)\) as \(T\to\infty\),
and symmetrically
\(\log\Lambda(T)\to-\log\operatorname{pr}(W=\operatorname{ess\,inf}W)\)
as \(T\to-\infty\). If instead \(W\) has no atom at \(M_W\), \(\Lambda\)
diverges: for a density behaving like \(c(M_W-x)^{\alpha}\) near
\(M_W\), \(\log\Lambda(T)=(\alpha+1)\log(T/2)+O(1)\). When \(W\) is
binary with \(\operatorname{pr}(W=1)=p\) the limit is approached from
below at an exponential rate,
\(\log\Lambda(T)=-\log p-2p^{-1}(1-p)e^{-T}\{1+o(1)\}\).
head: environment
name: An atom at the essential supremum

label: prp-dichotomy
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: The dichotomy

title: Proof
body_md:
For \emph{(i)} with \(\gamma_Y\to-\infty\),
\(e^{-w}=e^{-\gamma_X^{\mathrm{T}}X}e^{|\gamma_Y|Y}\), so
\(E(\pi_0e^{-kw})=e^{k|\gamma_Y|}\{A_k+o(1)\}\), the \(\{Y=0\}\) part
being exponentially negligible; the factors \(e^{2|\gamma_Y|}\) in
numerator and squared denominator cancel. Since
\(E(\pi_0e^{-kw})=e^{k|\gamma_Y|}A_k+B_k\) with
\(B_k=E\{\pi_0e^{-k\gamma_X^{\mathrm{T}}X}\mathbb 1(Y=0)\}\), Condition
\ref{def-mgf} is equivalent to \(A_k,B_k<\infty\), and \(A_1>0\) follows
from \(\operatorname{pr}(Y=1)>0\) with Condition \ref{def-overlap};
boundedness of \(\gamma_X(s)\) is what keeps \(A_k\) from drifting with
\(s\). Part \emph{(ii)} follows from Corollary~\ref{cor-sandwich}
applied to \(W=-w\) under the \(\pi_0\)-weighted law.
head: environment

label: lem-varprop
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Variance propagation under the response tilt

label: prp-rho-free
title: Proposition
body_md:
\protect\hypertarget{prp-rho-free}{}\label{prp-rho-free}

\(\Lambda(\gamma)\) is a functional of the law of \((X,Y)\) alone. In
particular it does not depend on the relevance \(\rho\) of the shadow
variable.
head: environment
name: \(\Lambda\) is free of the relevance

title: Proof
body_md:
By Theorem~\ref{thm-decomposition},
\(\Lambda(\gamma)=E(\pi_0e^{-2w})/\{E(\pi_0e^{-w})\}^{2}\) with
\(w=\gamma_X^{\mathrm{T}}X+\gamma_Y Y\); neither \(\pi_0\) nor \(w\)
involves \(Z\), so \(\Lambda\) is a functional of the law of \((X,Y)\),
and that law is free of \(\rho\) because (\ref{eq-relevance}) fixes the
conditional law of \(Z\) given \((X,Y)\) and leaves the marginal alone.
The shadow variable enters only through the moment condition that
identifies \(\gamma\), never through the weights.
head: environment

label: prp-quadratic
title: Proposition
body_md:
\protect\hypertarget{prp-quadratic}{}\label{prp-quadratic}

Let \(Q\) denote the \(\pi_0\)-weighted law and \(Q_s\) its tilt by
\(e^{sW}\), \(W=-w\), and let \(T=|\gamma_Y|\). If the tilted variance
converges, \(\operatorname{var}_{Q_s}(W)\to v_\infty\in(0,\infty)\) as
\(s\to\infty\), then \(\log\Lambda(T)/T^{2}\to v_\infty\).
head: environment
name: Quadratic growth

title: Proof
body_md:
By (\ref{eq-integral}), \(\log\Lambda(T)=\int_0^T(T-s)g(s)\,ds\) with
\(g(s)=4\operatorname{var}_{Q_{2s}}(W)-2\operatorname{var}_{Q_s}(W)\to2v_\infty\).
The kernel \((T-s)/T^{2}\) integrates to \(1/2\) over \([0,T]\) and puts
vanishing mass on any fixed initial segment. The substitution \(s=Tu\)
turns the left side into \(\int_0^1(1-u)g(Tu)\,du\), and \(g\) is
bounded---\(\operatorname{var}_{Q_s}(W)\) is continuous in \(s\) and
convergent---so the limit may be taken under the integral:
\(T^{-2}\int_0^T(T-s)g(s)\,ds\to2v_\infty\cdot\tfrac12=v_\infty\).
head: environment

label: thm-reach
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: The reach of the scan

title: Proof
body_md:
Requiring \(\mathrm{ESS}\ge m\) in (\ref{eq-ess}) gives
\(\operatorname{pr}(R=0)^{2}\Lambda\le n/m\), hence
\(\log\Lambda\le\log(n/m)-2\log\operatorname{pr}(R=0)\); substitute
Proposition~\ref{prp-quadratic}. The ceiling is immediate.
head: environment

label: lem-factorisation
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Factorization of the design matrix

label: thm-orders
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Orders in the relevance

label: thm-if
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Influence function and asymptotic normality

title: Proof
body_md:
The three orders of Theorem~\ref{thm-orders} have different sources. The
bias is
\(\|G_\lambda(\beta_0)\|=\lambda\|\Theta^{\mathrm{T}}q_\lambda\|\)
exactly, and by Lemma~\ref{lem-factorisation}
\(\|\Theta\|\asymp\rho^{-1}\) while \(q_\lambda\) is free of \(\rho\)
for \(\lambda\ll\sigma_{\min}(M)\), which gives \(\lambda/\rho\). The
condition number follows from \(M=\tilde MD\) with
\(D=\operatorname{diag}(I,\rho I)\), whose second block carries the
factor \(\rho\). The standard deviation is a consequence of
Theorem~\ref{thm-if} rather than a separate claim: in (\ref{eq-if}) the
factor \(a^{\mathrm{T}}q\) is free of \(\rho\) by
(\ref{eq-cancellation}), while the residual \(\psi(\beta_0)-\delta_0\)
carries \(\rho^{-1}\), because \(\delta_0=\Theta^{\mathrm{T}}b\) does;
hence \(\operatorname{var}(\mathrm{IF})\asymp\rho^{-2}\) and
\(\operatorname{sd}(\hat\beta_\lambda)\asymp n^{-1/2}\rho^{-1}\).
head: environment

label: thm-drifting
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: The local-to-zero limit is non-degenerate

title: Proof
body_md:
The \(Z\)-columns of \(\hat M\) are
\(\rho_n n^{-1}\sum R_ia_iS_ik_i^{\mathrm{T}}+(1-\rho_n^{2})^{1/2}n^{-1}\sum R_ia_i\nu_ik_i^{\mathrm{T}}\).
The first average converges to \(\tilde m=E(RaSk^{\mathrm{T}})\); the
second is centered, because \(\nu\) is independent of \((X,Y,R)\) with
mean zero, so it equals \(n^{-1/2}\xi_n\) with
\(\operatorname{vec}(\xi_n)\Rightarrow N(0,\Omega)\). With
\(\rho_n=c/n^{1/2}\) the whole block is \(n^{-1/2}\Psi_n\),
\(\Psi_n\Rightarrow\Psi\); the same computation on \(\hat v\) gives
\(n^{-1/2}\Phi_n\). Now \(\hat q\) solves
\(\hat M^{\mathrm{T}}\hat q=\hat v\). Blocking that system by the two
groups of columns of \(\hat M\) gives
\(A_n^{\mathrm{T}}\hat q=\hat v_0\) and
\(n^{-1/2}\Psi_n^{\mathrm{T}}\hat q=n^{-1/2}\Phi_n\): \textbf{the factor
\(n^{-1/2}\) appears on both sides of the second block and cancels
identically}, because both blocks inherit it from the single source
\(\rho_n\). The continuous mapping theorem applied to
\([A_n,\Psi_n]^{\mathrm{T}}\hat q=(\hat v_0,\Phi_n)\) gives
(\ref{eq-drifting}), the limit matrix being almost surely invertible by
the assumption on \(\Omega\). The convergence it needs is joint, and it
is: the summands behind \(\xi_n\) and \(\zeta_n\) do not involve
\(n\)---\(\rho_n\) only multiplies them---so a multivariate central
limit theorem applies to the two together, while \(A_n\) and
\(\hat v_0\) converge in probability to constants, which is all
Slutsky's theorem requires of them.
head: environment

label: prp-sievebias
title: Proposition
body_md:
\protect\hypertarget{prp-sievebias}{}\label{prp-sievebias}

If the sieve omits \(Zk_j(X)\), the approximation error is
\(e=(c_j/\rho)\{Zk_j-P_{\mathrm{ret}}(Zk_j)\}\), so
\(\|e\|\asymp\rho^{-1}\); nevertheless \(E\{(1-R)e\}=O(1)\) uniformly in
\(\rho\).
head: environment
name: The sieve bias is free of the relevance

label: lem-resolvent
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: How the ridge advances the small direction

label: prp-sdlambda
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: The standard deviation as a function of the ridge

label: def-M
title: Condition
body_md:
\protect\hypertarget{def-M}{}\label{def-M}

\(M\) is nonsingular; \(s:=\sigma_{\min}(M)>0\).
head: environment
name: Nonsingular design

label: def-rep
title: Condition
body_md:
\protect\hypertarget{def-rep}{}\label{def-rep}

The representer equation has a solution in the span of \(b\).
head: environment
name: Representer in the sieve

label: def-rep2
title: Condition
body_md:
\protect\hypertarget{def-rep2}{}\label{def-rep2}

The same holds for each column of
\(\partial\psi(\beta)/\partial\beta^{\mathrm T}\) in a neighborhood of
\(\beta_0\).
head: environment
name: Representer for the derivative

label: def-mom
title: Condition
head: environment
name: Fourth moments

label: def-diff
title: Condition
body_md:
\protect\hypertarget{def-diff}{}\label{def-diff}

\(\psi\) is continuously differentiable in \(\beta\) on a neighborhood
\(N\) of \(\beta_0\), with
\(\sup_{\beta\in N}\|\partial\psi(\beta)/\partial\beta^{\mathrm T}\|\le D\)
for a function \(D\) with \(ED^{4}<\infty\), and
\(H:=E\{\partial\psi(\beta_0)/\partial\beta^{\mathrm T}\}\) is

head: environment
name: Differentiability

label: def-cons
title: Condition
body_md:
\protect\hypertarget{def-cons}{}\label{def-cons}

\(\hat\beta_\lambda\to\beta_0\) in probability.
head: environment
name: Consistency

label: cor-atom-s
title: Corollary
body_md:
\protect\hypertarget{cor-atom-s}{}\label{cor-atom-s}

Let \(W\) have essential supremum \(M_W<\infty\) and
\(p:=\operatorname{pr}(W=M_W)>0\). Then \(\log\Lambda(T)\to-\log p\) as
\(T\to\infty\), and symmetrically
\(\log\Lambda(T)\to-\log\operatorname{pr}(W=\operatorname{ess\,inf}W)\)
as \(T\to-\infty\). If \(W\) has no atom at \(M_W\) and its density
behaves like \(c(M_W-x)^{\alpha}\) there, then
\(\log\Lambda(T)=(\alpha+1)\log(T/2)+O(1)\to\infty\). When \(W\) is
binary with \(\operatorname{pr}(W=1)=p\) the limit is approached from
below at an exponential rate,
\(\log\Lambda(T)=-\log p-2p^{-1}(1-p)e^{-T}\{1+o(1)\}\).
head: environment
name: An atom at the essential supremum

title: Proof
body_md:
With an atom, \(E(e^{tW})=pe^{tM_W}\{1+o(1)\}\) as \(t\to\infty\), so
\(K(t)=tM_W+\log p+o(1)\) and
\(\log\Lambda(T)=K(2T)-2K(T)=-\log p+o(1)\); the same computation
applied to \(-W\) gives the statement as \(T\to-\infty\). Without one,
Watson's lemma gives
\(E(e^{tW})=e^{tM_W}\Gamma(\alpha+1)c\,t^{-(\alpha+1)}\{1+o(1)\}\), so
\(K(t)=tM_W-(\alpha+1)\log t+O(1)\) and
\(\log\Lambda(T)=-(\alpha+1)\log(2T)+2(\alpha+1)\log T+O(1)=(\alpha+1)\log(T/2)+O(1)\).
For \(W\in\{0,1\}\) the first case applies with \(M_W=1\); the
monotonicity claimed in the main text follows from
\(f'(T)=2(p_{2T}-p_T)\) with \(p_t=pe^{t}/(1-p+pe^{t})\) strictly
increasing. The rate is exponential there: writing
\(g(t)=\log\{1+p^{-1}(1-p)e^{-t}\}\) we have \(K(t)=t+\log p+g(t)\), so
\[
  \log\Lambda(T)=K(2T)-2K(T)=-\log p+g(2T)-2g(T),
\] in which \(g(2T)=O(e^{-2T})\) is of smaller order while
\(g(T)=p^{-1}(1-p)e^{-T}\{1+o(1)\}\), whence
\(\log\Lambda(T)=-\log p-2p^{-1}(1-p)e^{-T}\{1+o(1)\}\). The term that
survives is the one carried over from \(-2K(T)\), so the limit is
approached from below, as the monotonicity just established requires.
This is the rate Section~\ref{sec-saturation} uses.
head: environment

label: lem-varprop-s
title: Lemma
body_md:
\protect\hypertarget{lem-varprop-s}{}\label{lem-varprop-s}

Let \(Y\mid X,Z\sim N(\mu,\varsigma^{2})\) and
\(\pi(y)=\operatorname{expit}(\gamma_0+\gamma_X^{\mathrm T}x+\gamma_Y y)\).
Then
\(\varsigma^{2}/(1+\gamma_Y^{2}\varsigma^{2}/4)\le\operatorname{var}(Y\mid R=1,X,Z)\le\varsigma^{2}\).
head: environment
name: Variance propagation

title: Proof
body_md:
Conditioning on \(R=1\) tilts the conditional law by \(\pi\), so its
density is \(p(y)\propto e^{-V(y)}\) with
\(V(y)=(y-\mu)^{2}/(2\varsigma^{2})-\log\operatorname{expit}(\gamma_0+\gamma_X^{\mathrm T}x+\gamma_Y y)\).
Since
\((d^{2}/dy^{2})\log\operatorname{expit}(\cdot)=-\gamma_Y^{2}\varpi(1-\varpi)\)
with \(\varpi=\operatorname{expit}(\cdot)\), \[
  V''(y)=\varsigma^{-2}+\gamma_Y^{2}\varpi(1-\varpi),\qquad
  \varsigma^{-2}\le V''\le \varsigma^{-2}+\gamma_Y^{2}/4,
\] using \(\varpi(1-\varpi)\le1/4\); in particular \(p\) is strongly
log-concave. The Brascamp--Lieb inequality, which for
\(p\propto e^{-V}\) with \(V''\ge m>0\) gives
\(\operatorname{var}_p(g)\le E_p\{(g')^{2}\}/m\), applied with
\(g(y)=y\) and \(m=\varsigma^{-2}\) yields the upper bound, strictly
when \(\gamma_Y\neq0\). For the lower bound apply the Cramér--Rao
inequality to the location family \(\{p(\cdot-t)\}\), for which \(Y\) is
unbiased for \(t\): \(\operatorname{var}_p(Y)\ge1/I(p)\) with
\(I(p)=E_p\{(V')^{2}\}=E_p(V'')\) by integration by parts, the boundary
terms vanishing by log-concavity, and
\(E_p(V'')\le \varsigma^{-2}+\gamma_Y^{2}/4\).
head: environment

label: lem-fact-s
title: Lemma
body_md:
\protect\hypertarget{lem-fact-s}{}\label{lem-fact-s}

\(M=\tilde MD\) with \(D=\operatorname{diag}(I,\rho I)\) and
\(\tilde M\) free of \(\rho\); consequently \(v^{\mathrm T}M^{-1}\) is
free of \(\rho\).
head: environment
name: Factorization

title: Proof
body_md:
Write \(b=(b^{0}(X),Zk(X))\). The \(Z\)-columns of \(M\) are
\(E\{RaZk(X)^{\mathrm T}\}=\rho E\{RaSk(X)^{\mathrm T}\}+(1-\rho^{2})^{1/2}E\{Ra\nu k(X)^{\mathrm T}\}\),
and the second term vanishes because \(a\) and \(k\) are
\((X,Y)\)-measurable while \(\nu\) is independent of \((X,Y,R)\) with
mean zero. The non-\(Z\) columns do not involve \(\rho\). The same
computation gives the \(Z\)-block of \(v\) as \(\rho E\{(1-\pi_0)Sk\}\).
Writing \(v=D\tilde v\) and \(M=\tilde MD\) gives
\(v^{\mathrm T}M^{-1}=\tilde v^{\mathrm T}DD^{-1}\tilde M^{-1}=\tilde v^{\mathrm T}\tilde M^{-1}\).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
\(M+\lambda I=M(I+\lambda M^{-1})\), so
\((M+\lambda I)^{-1}=(I+\lambda M^{-1})^{-1}M^{-1}\), the second factor
being invertible because every eigenvalue \(\mu\) of \(M\) has
\(|\mu|\ge\sigma_{\min}(M)=s\), so that \(-\lambda\) is not one of them
when \(\lambda<s\); this is what the hypothesis \(\lambda<s\) is for.
Now \(M^{-1}=\sum_k\sigma_k^{-1}v_ku_k^{\mathrm{T}}\), whose action is
dominated by \(s^{-1}v_1u_1^{\mathrm{T}}\) with the remainder bounded by
\(s_2^{-1}\); in particular
\(M^{-1}v_1=s^{-1}v_1(u_1^{\mathrm{T}}v_1)+O(s_2^{-1})\). Hence \(v_1\)
is an approximate eigenvector of \(M^{-1}\) with eigenvalue
\(\cos\theta/s\), and
\((I+\lambda M^{-1})^{-1}v_1=v_1\{1+\lambda\cos\theta/s\}^{-1}+O(\lambda/s_2)\).
Combining the two displays gives the resolvent law, equation
(\ref{eq-resolvent}) of the body above, the bound on \(E_\lambda\)
following from \(\sigma_2(M+\lambda I)\ge s_2-\lambda\) by Weyl's
inequality.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Write \(\hat\Theta_\lambda=(\hat M+\lambda I)^{-1}\hat r\) and expand
about the population value; the expansion is legitimate because
\(\|\hat M-M\|=o_p(s+\lambda\cos\theta)\), and gives
\(\hat\Theta_\lambda=\Theta_\lambda+(M+\lambda I)^{-1}(\Delta_r-\Delta_M\Theta_\lambda)+O_p(n^{-1})\).
Substituting into the sample criterion and collecting the mean-zero
terms replaces \(\Theta\) and \(w\) in the influence function
(\ref{eq-if}) by \(\Theta_\lambda\) and
\(q_\lambda=(M+\lambda I)^{-\mathrm{T}}v\). By the cancellation
(\ref{eq-cancellation}), \(q_\lambda\) is bounded uniformly in
\(\lambda\) and free of \(\rho\), so all of the \(\lambda\)-dependence
sits in \(\Theta_\lambda\) and in
\(\delta_{0,\lambda}=\Theta_\lambda^{\mathrm{T}}b\). By
(\ref{eq-resolvent}),
\(\Theta_\lambda=v_1(u_1^{\mathrm{T}}r)/(s+\lambda\cos\theta)+O(s_2^{-1})\),
so both carry the single scalar factor \((s+\lambda\cos\theta)^{-1}\)
and nothing else depending on \(\lambda\). Hence
\(\operatorname{var}(\mathrm{IF}_\lambda)=\tau^{2}(s+\lambda\cos\theta)^{-2}\{1+O(\lambda/s_2)\}\)
with \(\tau\) free of \(\lambda\), and the display follows on dividing
by the value at \(\lambda=0\). That \(\sigma_0^{2}\asymp1/(n\rho^{2})\)
is Theorem~\ref{thm-orders}.
head: environment

label: lem-neumann
title: Lemma
body_md:
\protect\hypertarget{lem-neumann}{}\label{lem-neumann}

Let \(A=M+\lambda I\), \(\hat A=A+\Delta_M\), \(0\le\lambda\le s/2\).
Then
\(\hat\Theta_\lambda-\Theta_\lambda=A^{-1}(\Delta_r-\Delta_M\Theta_\lambda)+\mathrm{Rem}\)
with
\(\mathrm{Rem}=-A^{-1}\Delta_MA^{-1}\Delta_r+A^{-1}\Delta_MA^{-1}\Delta_M\hat A^{-1}\hat r\),
and on \(\{\|\Delta_M\|\le s/4\}\), whose probability tends to one, \[
  \|\mathrm{Rem}\|\le 4s^{-2}\|\Delta_M\|\,\|\Delta_r\|+16s^{-3}\|\Delta_M\|^{2}\|\hat r\|=O_p(n^{-1}).
\]
head: environment
name: The Neumann remainder

title: Proof
body_md:
Iterating \((A+E)^{-1}=A^{-1}-A^{-1}E(A+E)^{-1}\) once gives the exact
identity \((A+E)^{-1}=A^{-1}-A^{-1}EA^{-1}+A^{-1}EA^{-1}E(A+E)^{-1}\);
multiply by \(\hat r=r+\Delta_r\) and cancel \(A^{-1}r=\Theta_\lambda\).
For the bound, \(\sigma_{\min}(A)\ge s-\lambda\ge s/2\), which is
positive by Condition~\ref{def-M}, so \(\|A^{-1}\|\le2/s\), and on the
stated event \(\sigma_{\min}(\hat A)\ge s/4\) so
\(\|\hat A^{-1}\|\le4/s\). By Condition~\ref{def-mom} and Chebyshev's
inequality \(\|\Delta_M\|\) and \(\|\Delta_r\|\) are \(O_p(n^{-1/2})\)
and \(\|\hat r\|=O_p(1)\).

title: Proposition
body_md:
\protect\hypertarget{prp-sieve-s}{}\label{prp-sieve-s}

If the sieve omits \(Zk_j(X)\) then
\(e=(c_j/\rho)\{Zk_j-P_{\mathrm{ret}}(Zk_j)\}\) and \(E\{(1-R)e\}=O(1)\)
uniformly in \(\rho\).
head: environment
name: Sieve misspecification

title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemma~\ref{lem-fact-s} the \(Z\)-block of \(\Theta\) is
\(\rho^{-1}c\) with \(c\) free of \(\rho\), so
\(\delta_0=\Theta_0^{\mathrm T}b^{0}+\rho^{-1}c^{\mathrm T}(Zk)\). The
retained sieve represents \(b^{0}\) and \(\{Zk_k:k\neq j\}\) exactly, so
the whole error is the omitted term projected off the retained span.
Writing
\(P_{\mathrm{ret}}(Zk_j)=\alpha^{\mathrm T}b^{0}+\sum_{k\neq j}\beta_kZk_k\),
\[
  E\{(1-R)e\}=\frac{c_j}{\rho}\Big[\rho E\{(1-\pi_0)Sk_j\}-\alpha^{\mathrm T}E\{(1-R)b^{0}\}
  -\rho\sum_k\beta_kE\{(1-\pi_0)Sk_k\}\Big].
\] The first and third terms carry \(\rho\). For the second, the normal
equations defining \(P_{\mathrm{ret}}\) have cross-blocks
\(E(b^{0}Zk^{\mathrm T})=\rho E(b^{0}Sk^{\mathrm T})\) and right-hand
side \(E(b^{0}Zk_j)=\rho E(b^{0}Sk_j)\), both \(O(\rho)\), whence
\(\alpha=O(\rho)\). If in addition \(Z\) is independent of \(X\) then
\(E\{Zk_j(X)b^{0}(X)\}=E\{E(Z\mid X)k_jb^{0}\}=0\) and \(\alpha\)
vanishes identically.
